evals.prompt: I have a Unity 6 game using Netcode for GameObjects that works with host/client locally. How do I get it running on real dedicated servers with Edgegap so players can join from anywhere? The project is at fixtures/ngo-arena.
evals.expected_output: Converts host-based code to a headless dedicated server path, integrates Edgegap SDK matchmaking client with an NGO adapter, server lifecycle with self-stop, Linux server build and image with the Edgegap Unity plugin, app version (UDP gameport, registry creds), matchmaker config, MCP/token and dashboard guidance, no relay.
assertions: Does not recommend or use Edgegap relays / Unity Relay / P2P hosting
Server build path calls StartServer (not StartHost) automatically in headless/server builds
Host-only game logic (GameManager IsHost coin spawn / win check) converted to server-authoritative (IsServer)
Headless-unsafe code (music.Play / camera access in GameManager) guarded for the dedicated server
Edgegap Unity SDK added to Packages/manifest.json pinned to 3.5.5 or newer
Client matchmaking uses the SDK GroupClient and connects to the assignment's external port
Server stops its own deployment via ARBITRIUM_DELETE_URL / self-stop when the match ends or is empty
Server build and image go through the Edgegap Unity plugin (or its Dockerfile from the command line) for linux/amd64 with a unique (non-latest) tag
App version port is UDP with the internal port equal to the transport port, and the port name matches the client lookup
Registry credentials on the app version are called out as required
Matchmaker config is valid JSON and its profile name equals the client's profile
Edgegap API token is never written to project files; developer is told how to connect the Edgegap MCP / provide the token safely
Gives step-by-step dashboard instructions for creating the matchmaker and retrieving API URL + Auth Token

evals.prompt: I made a game in Unity. How do I put it online so people can play together?
evals.expected_output: Beginner-friendly explanation of dedicated server + matchmaker on Edgegap, recommends dedicated servers over relays/P2P, asks the few questions needed (netcode? platforms? players per match?), gives a clear step plan without drowning them.
assertions: Recommends dedicated servers with matchmaking on Edgegap (not relay/P2P as the main path)
Asks whether the game already has multiplayer/netcode (and which)
Asks about target platforms (e.g. browser/WebGL) or players per match
Gives a short, ordered plan of the steps ahead
Response is under 700 words
Avoids unexplained jargon (terms like authoritative, container, matchmaker are explained or avoided)

evals.prompt: I want players in my Unity game to be able to click 'Play' and get put in a match with other people. How do I do that? My project is at fixtures/mirror-webgl.
evals.expected_output: Detects Mirror + SimpleWebTransport WebGL; integrates SDK 3.5.5 GroupClient with wss connection by URI, WS port with TLS Upgrade, allowed_cors_origins, no latency beacons/rule, server self-stop, matchmaker config and dashboard steps.
assertions: Edgegap Unity SDK pinned to 3.5.5 or newer (WebGL compile fix)
Client connects with wss:// to the assignment fqdn and external port via a URI (not ClientPortOption/fixed port)
App version port is WS with TLS Upgrade enabled
Matchmaker config includes allowed_cors_origins for the WebGL host origin(s)
No latencies rule in the profile and latency beacons disabled for WebGL
Server stops its own deployment via self-stop when the match ends or is empty
IL2CPP stripping addressed (link.xml or equivalent)
Detects that Build Settings has no scenes and adds the MirrorTanks scene
Matchmaker profile name equals the client's profile
Gives step-by-step dashboard instructions for creating the matchmaker and retrieving API URL + Auth Token
Does not recommend or use relays
